summary: I was sent back because O-002 landed on build-slice after my attempt 2 had passed. It is now listed as discharged, and no obligation is open against this stage. This attempt changes no files: `git diff --stat bd556e5 -- src tests eng` is empty. I re-ran the two tests that cover O-002's shape at this head, and both pass. `WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant StopDisabled` is a run where the scan finishes before the hook can act. Its hook log goes from 'waiting found=True enabled=False visible=True' to 'enabled=False visible=False' (the scan ended) to 'refused ... the app shut down first'. C-006 fails exactly once, on 'the hook acted' (hook never acted), with no ending mismatch reported. `WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-006` shows the large tree keeps its margin on a warm cache: the hook acted at 662 ms and the scan stopped at 550 of 30,150 folders.

obligations.how: No change was needed; I re-confirmed both tests at this head. `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant StopDisabled` feeds a run whose scan finishes before the hook acts: the hook sees the button disabled, then the panel collapse when the scan ends, then the app shutting down. The mutant passes only if C-006 fails on 'the hook acted' and nothing else, so a missing 'acted' line is reported as 'hook never acted' and not as an ending mismatch. `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-006` shows the committed New-LargeTree stays large enough on a warm cache: acted at 662 ms, stopped at 550 of 30,150 folders, ending Stopped.

cases.test_name: tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1::StopDisabled (the scan ends before the hook can act; C-006 must fail only on 'the hook acted')
tests/window/WindowCases.ps1::Test-C006 (New-LargeTree on a warm cache keeps the stop mid-scan)

follow_ups: The 'tree too small' version of O-002's shape has no deterministic committed feed. A small tree's scan opens a window of only a few milliseconds, against the hook's 25 ms poll, so the hook may or may not press Stop within it and a test built on that would be flaky. StopDisabled feeds 'the scan ended before the hook acted' by a different cause. The reporting it asserts does not depend on why the hook missed the scan.
